subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: What boundary should OpenClaw enforce for assistant-, plugin-, cron-, and shell-exec-initiated writes to protected exec and sandbox config settings?
rationale: The code has partial gateway-tool protection but still exposes model-visible config advice and a separate CLI-through-exec path; choosing whether to harden text, block CLI writes, add audit provenance, or require operator approval is a security/product boundary decision.

options.title: Require operator-approved protected writes
options.body: Remove model-visible protected config assignments and require explicit approval or clearly audited operator provenance before plugin, cron, or exec paths can write exec and sandbox config.

options.title: Ship text-only hardening first
options.body: Remove actionable config strings from assistant-facing sandbox errors while keeping the CLI-through-exec and plugin write boundary as a separate follow-up.

options.title: Keep current behavior with docs
options.body: Document that agents with host exec authority can run config CLI commands, accepting the current risk for high-trust deployments.

recommendation.title: Require operator-approved protected writes
recommendation.body: Remove model-visible protected config assignments and require explicit approval or clearly audited operator provenance before plugin, cron, or exec paths can write exec and sandbox config.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work touched both sandbox tool-policy auditing and gateway config-tool behavior, making this the closest current-main routing signal for the boundary decision.
